It also said it was working with rail unions, Network Rail and government officials to stabilise services and restore confidence in the franchise.

Politicians responded with a mixture of welcome and scepticism. Campaigners pointed out that many commuters had already lost trust in the operator after a long period of disruption, and said the profit announcement would ring hollow if timetables remained unpredictable.

Businesses also expressed concern, saying that unreliable rail links had damaged productivity, discouraged travel and made it harder for employees to reach workplaces, hospitals, colleges and client meetings.

Go-Ahead said it recognised that its reputation was tied directly to the experience of passengers travelling each day.
